questions.question: What is a water truck, and name three situations when water trucks are needed.
questions.expected_answer: A water truck, or water tanker, is a truck with a large tank that carries thousands of litres of water. It is needed in places without taps or other water sources nearby, such as some rural villages and informal settlements; during droughts; when pipes break or pumps stop; after floods; and at schools, clinics and hospitals when their supply stops.

questions.question: Describe two ways water trucks deliver water to a community.
questions.expected_answer: The truck fills large community tanks on stands, and people fill their containers from the tank's tap. Or the truck stops in the street and people fill their containers straight from its hose. Trucks often come on set days.

questions.question: Give three problems with getting water from water trucks, and say what the long-term answer is.
questions.expected_answer: Trucks can arrive late or not at all because of breakdowns or bad roads; they are expensive; each family gets only a limited amount; it is hard for elderly or sick people to carry water; the water can become dirty if tanks are not cleaned; trucks burn diesel and damage dirt roads. The long-term answer is dams, treatment works, pipes and taps.
